tests.name: parseAgentAccounts fills defaults and coerces missing fields
tests.evidence: An older managed-account index without optional identity/reauth/default fields must still load with null identities and reauth off; detects upgrade-induced account loss or spurious reauthentication.

tests.name: parseAgentAccounts rejects an unknown agent
tests.evidence: An unsupported agent identity must be refused instead of being launched as a supported provider; the otherwise-valid record isolates the agent enum.

tests.name: an older build's file round-trips: its toolset switches, unknown keys and grant families survive a rewrite untouched
tests.evidence: Authored legacy tool switches, future keys, unknown grant families and unreadable grant records must survive serialization verbatim; literal LEGACY comparison remains, parser-derived idempotence equality removed.

tests.name: grants keep working beside the legacy switches: a grant added and one revoked leave them untouched
tests.evidence: Adding/revoking an actual grant must preserve retired switches while ignoring their old enabled flag; catches grant edits destroying old-build state or disabling current authorization.

tests.name: missing fields read as defaults; a fresh file holds grants only
tests.evidence: Empty persisted input must grant nothing and a fresh serialized file must contain version 1 and an empty grants list; replaces equality to a production default factory with an independent empty-grants oracle.

tests.name: removing a thread drops its chat grants and its legacy rows — nothing else
tests.evidence: Deleting a thread must revoke its chat grants and old thread switches while preserving other threads and malformed legacy values; input immutability matters because callers share the read store.

tests.name: anything that is not a version-1 file throws, so the daemon moves it aside and grants read as none
tests.evidence: Unsupported outer versions/shapes must throw so callers quarantine rather than honor a damaged grant file; malformed legacy switches remain opaque.

tests.name: findGrant: only full-access, non workflow-owned callers; chat grants of that chat; project grants of that project
tests.evidence: Only full-access non-workflow callers may use matching chat/project grants; literal denied modes, cross-project unions, temporary/workspace targets and forbidden families catch privilege escalation.

tests.name: findGrant: workflows grants cover only the workflows recorded in that chat — never a create or a referenced prompt
tests.evidence: A workflows grant applies only to recorded workflow IDs and never creation, referenced prompts or another project; catches authorization widening despite a valid grant record.

tests.name: findGrant: a cross-project grant covers its one target project
tests.evidence: A cross-project grant authorizes exactly one recorded destination; catches target substitution or omitted-target authorization.

tests.name: lives beside daemon.json
tests.evidence: The remote login store must remain at daemon/auth-sessions.json across upgrades; a path change would silently invalidate devices and API tokens.

tests.name: unknown top-level keys and record fields survive a rewrite
tests.evidence: Known bearer digests/password fingerprint, unknown root/record fields and a nonexpiring API record must survive serialization; exact authored raw-file equality replaces parser-derived equality.

tests.name: records this build cannot read are kept verbatim and never honoured
tests.evidence: Unknown kinds, malformed bearer digests and duplicate digests must remain unreadable while surviving rewrite; catches acceptance of invalid credentials or rollback data loss.

tests.name: anything but a version-1 file throws
tests.evidence: An unsupported version/nonobject/nonlist must be refused rather than replacing login state; empty input remains a deliberately empty store.

tests.name: the usage-limit settings default to resume on, failover off — also for an app.json without them
tests.evidence: Legacy app preferences must resume limited chats by default but leave account failover off; explicit failover opt-in must survive parsing.

tests.name: a chat record's usage-limit state round-trips, keeping fields a newer daemon wrote
tests.evidence: The armed resume state, reset timestamp and newer failover metadata must survive session parsing; catches lost recovery scheduling after daemon restart.

tests.name: a malformed field falls back on its own; a block that does not parse is dropped, never the record
tests.evidence: Malformed recovery fields must individually fall back, and an unreadable recovery block must not discard the chat tab or its last sequence.

tests.name: desktop paths live under the daemon dir
tests.evidence: Desktop index/runtime directories must keep their documented daemon-owned paths so surviving desktops can be reconciled after restart.

tests.name: defaults are applied to desktop and app records
tests.evidence: Older desktop/app records must receive usable display defaults while a missing process status is never trusted as running; catches a false live-process claim from incomplete state.

tests.name: unknown record fields and top-level keys survive a parse/serialise round trip
tests.evidence: Unknown desktop/app/root fields and the recorded process group must survive serialization; literal field assertions replace production-derived parse-again equality.

tests.name: a VM desktop names its box and its directory there; older records run on this machine
tests.evidence: Box-backed desktops must preserve box identity/directory, old records remain local, and malformed box identity must be quarantined rather than misrouted locally.

tests.name: a bad record is kept verbatim in rejected while the good ones load
tests.evidence: Unreadable desktop records and repeated IDs must be retained verbatim beside independent valid desktop IDs; catches silent store loss and duplicate active owners.

tests.name: the outer shape still throws (quarantine, never overwrite)
tests.evidence: Outer version/list errors must refuse the whole store so the daemon quarantines it rather than overwrites surviving desktop metadata.

tests.name: size is clamped to the display bounds
tests.evidence: Persisted Xvnc dimensions must round and clamp to 320×240–7680×4320; these are process/resource input bounds, not incidental rendered geometry.

tests.name: recent launches are capped per project; unreadable entries are set aside, not used
tests.evidence: Recent launches must retain the first twenty valid entries per project, skip malformed commands, and avoid using unreadable project lists.

tests.name: unreadable recent entries are written back verbatim
tests.evidence: Unreadable recent-launch entries must survive serialization even while not offered as launch candidates; separate write obligation from the preceding read/cap contract.

tests.name: one unreadable app entry is kept verbatim and does not wipe the others
tests.evidence: A single unreadable app must not erase sibling apps, and its raw record must return to the serialized apps list without leaking the cache-only rejectedApps field.

tests.name: records keep the client's projectPath spelling beside the realpath
tests.evidence: Client project-path spelling must remain distinct from its realpath, allowing the UI project key and sandbox reconciliation to coexist; old records have no realpath hint.

tests.name: idle compaction defaults to T3 Code's 'when you return', also for an app.json without it
tests.evidence: Legacy app.json input must select onReturn and no account overrides, matching the documented user setting rather than enabling unattended compaction.

tests.name: a mode another version wrote reads as the default instead of failing the whole file
tests.evidence: An unknown global mode falls back, unreadable overrides alone disappear, and unrelated timeout preferences survive; catches one newer enum value corrupting the entire app config.

tests.name: an account's override wins over the default; an account without one follows it
tests.evidence: An explicit account override wins, otherwise the global mode applies, and inherited object keys must never become account overrides.

tests.name: an older client's whole `agents` write keeps the idle-compaction settings it does not know
tests.evidence: An older client updating another agents preference must preserve idle-compaction settings and unknown fields in the stored file; catches cross-version destructive writes.

tests.name: a field the body names wins, a record field is replaced whole, and an invalid update throws
tests.evidence: Explicit preference values win, the whole per-account record replaces prior entries so deletion works, invalid updates reject, and a first write can start from defaults.

tests.name: isValidName rejects traversal and empties
tests.evidence: Workspace/project names must reject hidden names, separators and empty/undefined values while permitting a normal project; catches traversal through public naming validation.

tests.name: a daemon.json written with the retired http.tailscaleServe flag still loads, the flag ignored
tests.evidence: A daemon config with the retired tailscaleServe field must remain usable while dropping that retired switch; catches a rollback-era file preventing daemon startup.

tests.name: sessionRecordSchema round-trips accountId so reattach keeps the account pin
tests.evidence: Persisted accountId must survive reattachment so a live account remains pinned and its refresh token is not rotated; older system sessions remain unpinned.

tests.name: sessionRecordSchema keeps a workflow owner and drops a malformed one, never the record
tests.evidence: Valid workflow/indexer ownership must survive parsing while malformed optional ownership alone is dropped; catches lost ownership or lost tabs on mixed-version metadata.

tests.name: assertInsideFsRoot allows in-root paths and rejects escapes
tests.evidence: The real filesystem containment API must accept existing/new in-root paths and throw FsSandboxError for escapes; the temp directory is necessary to exercise realpath behavior.

tests.name: legacy proxy-home tabs and thread heads remain readable after launcher retirement
tests.evidence: Retired cliproxy tabs/heads must remain readable as system-home records with resume identity intact; catches losing stored conversations after launcher retirement.

tests.name: a head written before goals — no marker — still parses, and says no
tests.evidence: A pre-goals head must remain readable without adding an automatic goal-resume marker; catches unintended autonomous work after upgrade.

tests.name: a malformed goal-resume marker is dropped, never the whole head
tests.evidence: Non-true goal-resume markers must be dropped without losing the thread; catches malformed state triggering automatic continuation.

tests.name: a head without the goal-hold marker says no, and writes none back
tests.evidence: An old head must omit the goal-hold marker on rewrite; catches an upgrade inventing a held goal.

tests.name: a malformed goal-hold marker is dropped, never the whole head
tests.evidence: A malformed goal-hold marker must be dropped independently; catches one optional handover value making the whole thread unreadable.

tests.name: a stamped continuation marker round-trips beside both goal marks — through JSON, as meta.json holds it
tests.evidence: An explicitly authored stamped continuation and both true goal markers must survive parsing; prevents losing automatic handover intent. Removes parse-again equality whose expected value came from production.

tests.name: the crash-resume count round-trips on the marker and the head — through JSON, as meta.json holds it
tests.evidence: Literal crashAttempt and crashResumedTurn values must survive parsing, preventing a crash loop from losing its retry limit; removes a production-derived idempotence equality.

tests.name: a pending wake round-trips on the head through JSON; a bad one reads as none, a bad task is dropped
tests.evidence: A literal completed-task wake must survive, malformed tasks alone disappear and invalid wake state falls back; catches losing deferred task results. Removes a derived parse-again equality.

tests.name: a malformed crash-resume count reads as none, never an unreadable head
tests.evidence: Invalid nonpositive/noninteger crash counts must disappear without losing the continuation turn or thread; catches corrupt retry state disabling recovery.

tests.name: a malformed continuation stamp reads as unstamped — an older host's marker — never an unreadable head
tests.evidence: An unreadable continuation stamp must leave its turn/prepared flag usable under the legacy rule and preserve unrelated handover state; catches unreadable threads or wrong restart policy.

tests.name: daily log files: a day's first file, its later parts, and parsing them back
tests.evidence: Daily log paths must use local calendar day plus documented part suffixes, and parser must reject unrelated/ambiguous filenames; catches wrong-day logs and retention deleting unrelated files.

tests.name: a bad field costs that field only; unknown fields and records survive
tests.evidence: Unreadable linking fields and list elements must fall back independently while valid state, unknown keys and counters survive; catches one malformed value losing all indexer state.

tests.name: not a version-1 object throws (the caller keeps the file aside)
tests.evidence: The version-1 parser must refuse unsupported versions and primitives so callers do not overwrite unreadable state.

tests.name: a newer version's state reads what this build knows and keeps its version and unknown fields on rewrite
tests.evidence: A newer linking state whose known values remain readable must retain its own version and unknown data through an actual edited serialization; catches destructive downgrade writes.

tests.name: a newer version's state with a known field this build cannot read is not intact
tests.evidence: A newer state with any unreadable known field/list member must be flagged nonintact; catches an older daemon rewriting and discarding newer state.

tests.name: readKnowledgeLinkingState: a current file reads as current; an older, odd or missing version still throws
tests.evidence: The compatibility reader must distinguish current state from unsupported old/noninteger/missing versions; catches incorrectly adopting a file that must be quarantined.

tests.name: ids follow the contract's shapes
tests.evidence: Entry file-name predicates must accept the literal lowercase twelve-character entry ID and refuse uppercase/short stems used by graph/search file discovery; collection-ID checks move to the real collection parser and its dead wrapper is removed.

tests.name: collections file: unknown fields, unreadable records and unknown keys survive a rewrite
tests.evidence: Collections must retain unknown data/unreadable rows, reject repeated names/IDs and overlong IDs, and serialize an unknown color unchanged; adds literal neon serialization assertion from the consolidated color case.

tests.name: collections file: a colour this build does not know (a newer palette key) is kept for the rewrite
tests.evidence: The standalone newer-color setup duplicates unknown-color preservation in the collections rewrite owner; its only distinct default-color assertion moves into the existing bare-array compatibility case.
tests.survivor: Same file: collections rewrite owner + bare-array compatibility owner

tests.name: collections file: a bare array reads as version 1; a wrong outer shape throws
tests.evidence: Legacy bare arrays must remain readable, absent colors default to chart-1, empty stores remain empty and invalid outer shapes refuse rewrite; protects actual old disk shapes without a separate color scenario.

tests.name: entry frontmatter: defaults, tolerated variants, and unknown keys kept
tests.evidence: Entry frontmatter must normalize legacy savedFrom/empty author, default optional metadata and refuse missing content hash/invalid ID while preserving unknown keys.

tests.name: entry frontmatter: savedFrom keeps unknown keys, and an unknown `by` still reads
tests.evidence: A newer savedFrom identity or unknown nested metadata must survive parsing; catches silently losing provenance when opening entries saved by another version.

tests.name: a tab record keeps its lineage, and drops one it cannot read — never the record
tests.evidence: Tab records retain valid parent/fork lineage, while malformed optional lineage never costs the tab and old tabs remain parentless.

tests.name: a fork point that does not read is dropped on its own
tests.evidence: An unreadable fork point alone must disappear without losing the parent/relation; detects overly coarse optional-field rejection.

tests.name: the head keeps its lineage, and a malformed one reads as none
tests.evidence: Thread heads independently retain lineage or drop only unreadable lineage; the head and session index use separate persisted schemas.

tests.name: the fork handoff reads whole or not at all
tests.evidence: Fork handoff must preserve transcript and optional deliveredTurnId/unknown fields while refusing unsupported version or empty transcript; malformed delivery markers must not lose the transcript.

tests.name: the merge outbox keeps unreadable entries and unknown fields for the next rewrite
tests.evidence: Merge outbox must preserve unreadable rows, unknown fields and failed-attempt state, default legacy states, and refuse bad outer shapes; prevents dropped/replayed queued merges after restart.

tests.name: a lineage's delegation depth persists, and a bad one is dropped on its own
tests.evidence: Delegation depth must survive or be dropped independently when unreadable; catches depth limits silently resetting after restart.

tests.name: a queued merge keeps its plan mode; an unknown mode is dropped, never the merge
tests.evidence: Queued plan interaction mode must survive, while an unknown optional mode never loses the merge; catches restart changing the intended execution mode.

tests.name: a tab record keeps an `opened` lineage and `agentCreated: true`; any other agentCreated is dropped on its own
tests.evidence: Opened lineage and true agentCreated must survive, while malformed ownership alone disappears; catches a chat losing its agent-created authority identity.

tests.name: the delivery queue: merge, reply and message entries; an unknown kind is kept verbatim, never delivered as a merge
tests.evidence: The delivery queue must distinguish merge/reply/message, retain unknown kinds as unreadable and preserve cause/subscription metadata; catches delivering an unknown kind as a merge.

tests.name: the reply outbox round-trips and keeps unknown fields, unknown states and unreadable entries verbatim
tests.evidence: Reply outbox must preserve valid subscriptions/deliveries, unknown raw state, duplicate rows and root fields on serialization; catches cross-chat delivery loss during upgrades.

tests.name: a subscription keeps its idempotency key and its retry-stable queue entry
tests.evidence: Idempotency and stable queue-entry IDs must survive persistence, and a malformed idempotency key makes only its subscription unreadable; catches duplicated delivery after retry.

tests.name: the reply outbox refuses anything but a version-1 outbox
tests.evidence: Reply outbox rejects unsupported outer shapes, defaults absent interaction mode, and drops only an unknown origin; catches unsafe rewrites or misrouted origin state.

tests.name: the new stores live beside the merge outbox
tests.evidence: Reply, tool-grant and approval-journal files must keep their documented daemon-owned paths across upgrades.

tests.name: a lineage keeps the inherited `workflowOwned: true`; any other value is dropped on its own
tests.evidence: Inherited true workflowOwned must survive lineage parsing while other values do not create inherited workflow ownership; catches a delegated chat escaping workflow restrictions.

tests.name: a subscription's posted / ended / toTitle round-trip; a newer ending is kept, a malformed post makes the entry unreadable
tests.evidence: Posted receipt, ending and destination title must survive, unknown future endings are preserved, and malformed posted receipt quarantines the entry; catches duplicate post after restart.

tests.name: the reply outbox's attention notices round-trip, an unreadable one kept verbatim; an outbox without them writes none
tests.evidence: Attention notices must retain retry/cause metadata and unknown fields, keep unreadable notices verbatim and remain absent from old empty outboxes; catches lost pending-input notifications.

tests.name: plugin files live in the daemon dir
tests.evidence: Plugin config, install and preload paths must preserve the on-disk daemon layout so existing installations and launch preloads remain discoverable.

tests.name: a ts-rust record with an engine and tsrs's versions round-trips; a record without them still reads
tests.evidence: The same real plugin record now protects both legacy top-level tsc-rs versions/check/error fields and nested tsrs versions; literal full-record equality catches selective field loss, while old records keep no inferred engine.

tests.name: an engine this build does not know reads as none and is kept; a malformed tsrs record is rejected
tests.evidence: Unknown engine selections remain raw but are not used; malformed nested tsrs install state must reject at use, preventing a newer engine name corrupting all plugin state.

tests.name: an empty plugins.json reads as no plugin state
tests.evidence: Empty plugin config and missing known-plugin records must be read as no enabled/install state; catches spontaneous activation or inability to start with no plugins.

tests.name: a full plugin record round-trips
tests.evidence: Top-level installed/previous/skipped/check/error fields are merged into the stronger two-engine record owner; removes a second otherwise-equivalent parse/pluginStateOf roundtrip.
tests.survivor: Same file: a ts-rust record with an engine and tsrs's versions round-trips; a record without them still reads

tests.name: an older build's per-workspace list is read as it is, and never defaulted in
tests.evidence: Legacy per-workspace activation remains stored verbatim and is never invented for current enabled records; catches breaking rollback/migration activation state.

tests.name: unknown fields and unknown plugin ids written by other versions are kept
tests.evidence: Unknown root, install, record and plugin fields must survive; known knowledge settings passthrough now shares this owner and still checks the actual pluginStateOf output against literal settings.

tests.name: an unknown plugin id with any shape does not make the file unreadable, and round-trips verbatim
tests.evidence: An unknown plugin may have a wholly different/primitive shape without poisoning known-plugin reads; generic unknown object fields alone do not protect this case.

tests.name: a malformed plugins.json is rejected rather than read as empty
tests.evidence: Malformed plugin outer versions/list shapes must reject rather than masquerade as an empty installation state.

tests.name: a known plugin's malformed record is rejected where it is read
tests.evidence: A malformed known-plugin activation/install record must reject only where used; catches launching or overwriting untrustworthy plugin state.

tests.name: knowledge-graph settings read field by field; a bad value never makes the record unreadable
tests.evidence: Knowledge settings must accept only readable account/model/concurrency fields individually, keeping nullable legacy selection and ignoring bad values without losing the plugin.

tests.name: knowledge-graph settings read the account policy field by field, keeping unknown keys
tests.evidence: Knowledge account policies must preserve literal valid strategy/limits, apply independent defaults and tolerate unknown keys/list items field by field; catches unintended indexing account selection.

tests.name: a plugin record's settings and their unknown keys survive a parse
tests.evidence: Known-plugin settings and unknown metadata passthrough move into the existing unknown-fields owner; no settings-preservation assertion is dropped.
tests.survivor: Same file: unknown fields and unknown plugin ids written by other versions are kept

tests.name: the store and its icons live beside the other daemon-owned indexes
tests.evidence: Repository identity index and icon directory must keep documented daemon-owned paths so existing labels/icons remain accessible.

tests.name: a well-formed store round-trips unchanged
tests.evidence: Authored emoji, PNG/favicon and absent-icon records must all parse unchanged, including optional labels/source metadata; catches supported identity variants disappearing.

tests.name: unknown fields survive, at every level
tests.evidence: Unknown root, identity, image and favicon-source fields must survive; protects rollback data across all nested identity layers.

tests.name: bad entries are set aside one by one, verbatim; the rest loads
tests.evidence: Unreadable identity/icon records, unsafe filenames, unsupported media and malformed metadata must be quarantined verbatim while a valid sibling loads; catches unsafe icon reads or whole-store loss.

tests.name: a repeated repoKey: the first record is the identity, the later one is kept aside
tests.evidence: A repeated repo key must preserve the first identity and retain the later raw row; catches nondeterministic identity selection or data loss.

tests.name: a missing list or version reads as an empty version-1 store
tests.evidence: A legacy empty object must remain an empty version-1 identity store rather than an unreadable file.

tests.name: a broken outer shape throws, so the daemon moves the file aside
tests.evidence: Unsupported outer versions/shapes must refuse rewriting rather than wipe repository labels/icons.

tests.name: icon file names are generated ids only
tests.evidence: The filename guard used for actual icon reads/deletes must accept supported generated IDs/extensions and refuse traversal, separators, case/extension changes and oversized names.

tests.name: repoIconFileOfEntry reads a well-formed file name off any entry, rejected ones included
tests.evidence: Garbage collection must recover a safe referenced image filename even from a rejected/future identity without treating unsafe or nonrecord data as a file; catches deleting another version’s still-referenced icon.

tests.name: savedPromptsPath lives beside the other daemon-owned indexes
tests.evidence: The saved library must remain at daemon/saved-prompts.json so upgrades do not silently hide user prompts.

tests.name: a well-formed library round-trips unchanged
tests.evidence: Fails unique-protection bar: the repository-scope case already compares the same complete authored legacy/project/global records, and the empty-store case checks rejected/extra defaults. Remove this duplicate parser success setup.

tests.name: bad entries are set aside one by one, verbatim; the rest of the library loads
tests.evidence: Unreadable saved prompt records must be retained verbatim without dropping valid siblings; catches one corrupt prompt wiping the library.

tests.name: a repeated id keeps its first record; the others are set aside, not dropped
tests.evidence: Repeated IDs keep the first prompt and retain later raw rows; catches a duplicate replacing a user’s saved content.

tests.name: repository scope round-trips, accepts legacy records, and preserves invalid entries
tests.evidence: Complete legacy/project/repository/global prompt records must survive parsing while malformed repository scope is quarantined; this is the stronger owner of the deleted generic well-formed case.

tests.name: unknown top-level keys are kept, exactly as found
tests.evidence: Unknown root keys, including __proto__, remain own data rather than object inheritance; catches prototype pollution or rollback data loss.

tests.name: optional fields default, limits are NOT re-applied, and unknown fields pass through
tests.evidence: Older prompt defaults, longer stored title/tag lists and unknown record fields must survive without reapplying current editor limits; catches rollback hiding user content.

tests.name: the outer shape still throws — an unknown version included — so the file is not rewritten
tests.evidence: Unsupported library version/nonlist shape refuses rewriting, while an empty object is a deliberate empty library; catches destructive fallback.

tests.name: createdBy survives a read and a rewrite verbatim — newer kinds and fields too; a non-object makes the record unreadable, kept verbatim
tests.evidence: Agent-created provenance and unknown future kinds/fields must survive, malformed nonobjects are quarantined and old prompts remain user-owned; catches unauthorized ownership reinterpretation.

tests.name: a null createdBy reads (and is rewritten) as absent; only a structurally invalid non-null value sets the record aside
tests.evidence: Explicit null provenance must behave as absent while invalid arrays/empty objects quarantine records; catches older null-valued prompts disappearing or being misclassified.

tests.name: the vault index and its blobs live under daemon/secret-files
tests.evidence: Vault index/blob directories must keep their daemon/secret-files layout, preserving stored private-file content references across upgrades.

tests.name: a well-formed index round-trips unchanged
tests.evidence: Fails unique-protection bar: complete vault bytes already round-trip in unknown-fields and retired-files/legacy-record owners, while the duplicate-key case independently retains multiple workspaces. Remove repeated success-only parse/serialize setup.

tests.name: an empty or default file parses to no vaults; missing excluded/clones default
tests.evidence: Legacy empty/default vaults and missing exclusion/clone maps must still load without invented files or clone baselines.

tests.name: unknown fields survive at every level, and unknown top-level keys are kept
tests.evidence: Unknown nested version/provenance/file/clone/root metadata must survive actual serialization exactly; catches destructive rollback rewrites of private-file history.

tests.name: bad records are set aside one by one, verbatim, and written back after the good ones
tests.evidence: Invalid paths, hashes, version IDs and record shapes must remain quarantined beside valid vaults; version boundary/separator checks move here from the removed test-only predicate, and a valid minimum-length version remains in the common authored fixture.

tests.name: retired files and unlisted clones round-trip; records without them still parse
tests.evidence: Retired histories and unlisted clone timestamps must survive, older records gain no retired data, and a formerly retired path may be managed again; catches lost restore histories or broken remanagement.

tests.name: a repeated (workspace, repoKey) keeps the first and sets the rest aside
tests.evidence: Duplicate workspace/repository keys must preserve the first vault while a different workspace remains usable; catches cross-workspace vault collision.

tests.name: the outer shape throws
tests.evidence: Unsupported outer versions/shapes must refuse rewrite, preventing a damaged vault index from being replaced with empty state.

tests.name: a __proto__ key in a stored map stays an own key and pollutes nothing
tests.evidence: An own __proto__ clone/root key must round-trip without polluting Object.prototype; catches attacker-controlled map keys changing object behavior or losing clone baselines.

tests.name: the record schema and the id predicates
tests.evidence: Actual blob-file guard must accept lowercase SHA-256 and reject trailing newline/traversal. Remove the duplicate successful record-schema assertion and dead version-predicate wrapper; its meaningful version checks move to persisted-record rejection.

tests.name: reads good items, keeps bad ones verbatim with a reason, and round-trips unknown fields
tests.evidence: Manifest must load good skills/MCP, report unreadable/new-kind/duplicate items in place, and preserve unknown root/settings/item/MCP metadata on serialization.

tests.name: defaults what an older or hand-written manifest leaves out
tests.evidence: Handwritten/older manifests must receive empty description/settings and enabled/all-agent defaults without losing their command item.

tests.name: keeps a setting it cannot read verbatim through a rewrite, never failing the profile
tests.evidence: Unknown-shaped known settings must remain completely raw across rewrite; catches an older build coercing a newer setting and permanently losing it.

tests.name: knowledgeCollections (Knowledge Graph): absent is fine; a list, stale ids or an unreadable value round-trip verbatim
tests.evidence: Knowledge collection references, including stale or unreadable values, must remain opaque and absent when omitted; catches profile rewrite dropping collection restrictions or inventing selection.

tests.name: keeps a plugin source it cannot read verbatim through a rewrite; reads it only at use
tests.evidence: Unknown plugin source formats must survive rewrite but remain unreadable at use, while a supported marketplace source retains future metadata; prevents loading an unsupported source as something else.

tests.name: throws on anything that is not a version-1 manifest
tests.evidence: Unsupported manifest versions and unsafe profile IDs must refuse the entire manifest; catches rewriting incompatible profiles or escaping profile directories.

tests.name: round-trips readable entries, unreadable ones and unknown keys
tests.evidence: Profile-secret records must preserve readable values, unreadable item rows and root keys; empty files serialize with no secrets, preventing secret loss during mixed-version writes.

tests.name: never quotes a value when it throws
tests.evidence: Unsupported secret-file versions must throw without including the supplied secret in the error message; independently authored s3cret is forbidden output.

tests.name: round-trips readable entries, unreadable ones and unknown keys; refuses another version
tests.evidence: Deleted-profile names and unreadable tombstones/unknown fields must survive rewrite, with unsupported versions refused and the documented deleted-index path unchanged.

tests.name: lays the profiles, prepared and staging dirs under <appdir>/daemon/session-profiles
tests.evidence: Profile source, prepared account/version and staging directories must keep their documented layout; unsafe prepared version segments must throw before path construction.

tests.name: keys the system identity as `system` and refuses unsafe segments
tests.evidence: System account identity must map to system while opaque IDs remain unchanged and unsafe profile path segments reject; catches profile/account directory escape.

tests.name: keeps a profileId on the tab's chat block and drops one that does not read
tests.evidence: The session-index chat schema must retain valid profileId, omit absent values and drop malformed IDs; catches a restart silently losing the launch profile.

tests.name: keeps a profileId on the thread head (the schema strips unknown keys)
tests.evidence: The separately persisted thread head must retain valid profileId and drop blank/absent values; head parsing strips unknown keys, so a session-record assertion cannot supersede this one.

tests.name: the subagent cache lifetime defaults to auto
tests.evidence: Old app config/default preferences must select automatic TTL rather than change billing/cache behavior after upgrade.

tests.name: each subagent cache lifetime mode is preserved and anything else is rejected
tests.evidence: The three supported TTL modes must remain selectable while unsupported strings/nonstring values reject; catches malformed persisted policy silently taking effect.

tests.name: the auto decision is kept in the daemon dir
tests.evidence: The automatic decision file must keep its daemon/subagent-cache-ttl.json path so previously computed policy remains available.

tests.name: a stored auto decision round-trips
tests.evidence: An authored automatic decision must retain TTL/timestamps/outcome/request count/cost estimate, including an insufficient-data null estimate; catches losing persisted adaptation state.

tests.name: a stored auto decision that cannot be trusted reads as none
tests.evidence: Unreadable or unsupported automatic decisions must read as none; catches applying an untrusted TTL or timestamp to future launches.

tests.name: box tooling paths follow the target's separators
tests.evidence: Tooling/install/archive paths must follow the target OS separators and documented cache layout, regardless of daemon OS; catches a Windows box receiving unusable POSIX paths.

tests.name: Node loads preloads with backslashes, spaces and quotes while preserving existing options
tests.evidence: One real Node child must load authored preload filenames with backslashes/spaces/quotes and retain an existing --title; stdout is an independent interoperability oracle, not a mocked tokenizer.

tests.name: PATH: prepended with the target's delimiter; Windows merges every spelling into the one present
tests.evidence: PATH contributions must preserve target delimiters/order, merge Windows key spellings case-insensitively, leave POSIX Path separate and refuse to hide the original PATH.

tests.name: env vars land under the existing spelling on Windows; the input env is never changed
tests.evidence: Windows environment contributions must honor an existing variable spelling without mutating input; catches a child receiving duplicate case-variant env keys or shared launch state being overwritten.

tests.name: no contribution leaves the env as it is; requiring the same file twice adds it once
tests.evidence: An empty contribution is a no-op and repeated preload contributions must be idempotent; catches duplicate preload side effects across overlapping plugins.

tests.name: legacy claude/codex booleans migrate into agents record
tests.evidence: Legacy per-agent usage booleans must migrate preserving both enabled and disabled choices; catches an upgrade turning monitoring back on.

tests.name: new agents record passes through
tests.evidence: Explicit new per-agent opt-out must apply while an unspecified agent remains enabled; catches unknown/new agent handling overriding existing preferences.

tests.name: disabled master switch overrides per-agent
tests.evidence: The master usage switch must override an individual enabled agent; catches monitoring continuing after the user disables it.

tests.name: usage defaults and legacy app migration preserve supported chip preferences
tests.evidence: Legacy app/default chip preferences must retain busiest/default enable and allow the supported Grok chip while rejecting unknown chip IDs.

tests.name: agent block profileId (Agent Profiles §5.5): kept by id, absent = Global, unknown fields survive
tests.evidence: An explicit workflow profileId and unknown future config fields must persist, while omitted profileId remains Global; catches unattended runs losing their chosen profile.

tests.name: agent block profileId: a blank or non-string id fails the block, so the record is set aside verbatim — never run as Global
tests.evidence: A malformed explicit profileId must quarantine that whole workflow record while a valid sibling remains usable; catches silently running a broken explicit profile as Global.

survivingCrossPackageConsolidations.name: Claude stream timeout defaults to 30 minutes and accepts only whole minutes from 1 to 30
survivingCrossPackageConsolidations.evidence: Surviving lowest owner of apps/daemon/src/agent-timeout-config.test.ts (three baseline scenarios): defaults to literal 30; accepts literal endpoints 1/30; refuses 0/31/noninteger/numeric string. The Settings input and independent UI default specify the range/default; config schema is the lowest stable boundary and daemon launch reads it. No new behavioral contract is invented.

validation.baseline: Original central baseline: all 147 config tests passed in 19 file summaries.
validation.performance: No isolated speedup claimed. This package has no sleeps/browser/server setup; one real Node preload subprocess and one realpath fixture remain because the external process/filesystem interfaces are the contracts.
